A1.justification: Both PDFs describe PerLDiff and provide readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. The retained material can be matched despite substantial reformatting and appendix reorganization.

before.justification: v3 reports original NuScenes and KITTI generation evaluations, synthetic-data augmentation results, component ablations, and qualitative experiments.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results and adds a comparison of road-map encoders.

M1.justification: The proposed condition encoders, perspective masks, gated attention, view/text attention, and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged. ConvNext remains the default road encoder; the CLIP alternative is an ablation. Frozen ConvNext weights were already indicated in v3 Figure 2.

E1.justification: Both versions retain NuScenes and KITTI, multi-view and monocular detection, BEV segmentation, synthetic-data augmentation, and the same orientation, weather, and temporal examples. The encoder ablation adds no dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: v4 Table 2 omits the published MagicDrive segmentation comparator present in v3 Table 1, while retaining MagicDrive*. v4 Table 7 adds a CLIP-image-encoder alternative to ConvNext. The existing detection comparator sets remain intact.

E3.justification: v4 Table 7 introduces a controlled comparison of frozen road encoders with different sizes, evaluated through BEVFormer and BEVFusion. Existing splits, resolutions, training budgets, and sampling settings are retained. The ControlNet comparison now reports detection metrics without its previous segmentation metrics.

E4.justification: Section 4.3.3 and Table 7 newly test sensitivity to the road-map encoder. The existing mask, masking-weight, CFG, view-attention, MagicDrive-mask, and ControlNet analyses remain, although the ControlNet ablation loses its CVT segmentation evidence.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. v4's new '±0.02 NDS' statement describes a difference between encoders, not statistical uncertainty.

E6.justification: v4 Table 7 adds CLIP-encoder results: FID 12.77 and NDS 36.26 with BEVFormer and 24.45 with BEVFusion. Removed segmentation entries include MagicDrive's 61.05/27.01 and the second oracle's 70.46/35.86 from v3 Table 1, plus ControlNet's 53.98/24.72 from v3 Table 9. Retained numerical results match across versions.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, attention computations, DDPM preliminaries, and Algorithm 1 are retained. Splitting v3 Equation 5 into v4 Equations 5–6 changes presentation only; no assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about geometric-prior control, PerL-based attention, NuScenes/KITTI performance, and potential traffic-simulation applications. Added novelty adjectives do not change their scientific scope.

C2.justification: Section 4.3.3 newly motivates ConvNext through compactness and edge-feature extraction and interprets encoder choice as having little effect. Its '±0.02 NDS' summary fits BEVFormer but overlooks Table 7's 0.40 BEVFusion gap. Existing orientation failures and background-fidelity limitations remain.

D1.justification: v4 discloses encoder parameter counts of 27.82M for ConvNext and 303.97M for CLIP, together with the frozen-weight ablation setup. Appendix B retains the hardware, optimization, training-duration, and sampling details; the repository link is unchanged.

R1.justification: The same 41 referenced works and substantive positioning against prior generation and geometric-control methods are retained. Switching from author–year to numbered citations does not change research positioning.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main narrative remain intact. v4 makes local wording edits, uses numbered experimental subsections and bulleted contributions, adds acknowledgements, moves limitations into Appendix C, and reorders supplementary analyses.

P2.justification: v4 replaces the single-column layout with two columns, splits and transposes the detection/segmentation table, and adds the encoder table. It redesigns the introductory and KITTI comparisons to display conditioning layouts, extensively resizes and relabels figures, and relocates failure and weather illustrations.

improvement.justification: The added encoder ablation provides a limited empirical basis for choosing the much smaller ConvNext encoder with similar reported detection scores, while explicit conditioning diagrams clarify the examples. The gains are modest: core results remain unchanged, some segmentation comparisons disappear, and the new NDS summary incorrectly generalizes the BEVFormer gap to BEVFusion.
